key_insight: PING combines graph neural networks with advection–diffusion physics to forecast transport on irregular sensor networks and support improved solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: More accurate intra-day PV power forecasts can support grid integration of solar generation rather than improve solar-cell efficiency directly.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on an irregular graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-sensor measurements and satellite-derived cloud information.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting through the hybrid approach.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical gains or deployment costs, so practical benefits require validation on the target PV network.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
